q7.answer: The secret holder in process memory keeps the current value. A refresh (the 5-minute timer in R3, or the immediate refresh on a 401/403 in R4) swaps in the new version with one reference assignment. Each provider call reads the key from the holder when the request is built, not from a copy in the client, so the next call uses the new key. Calls already in flight keep the value they read.

q8.answer: Step 10 is the gate. Every pod must report the new version id for all three secrets through a metric or structured log that carries no values. No pre-migration pod may still be running, since those read keys from the old image and report no store version. Provider dashboards must show zero requests on the old keys. The team must wait one full 5-minute refresh cycle plus the 10-second payment timeout, then observe for 15 minutes with error rates at baseline. Any pod still on an old version id blocks Step 12.

q9.answer: Order: (1) Step 2, set up store paths, KMS keys and IAM so orders-api-prod can read only orders-api/prod/* and engineers have no prod read. (2) Step 3, issue new keys at each provider while the old keys stay valid. (3) Steps 4 and 5, write the new prod keys and the dev keys to the store. (4) Step 6, merge the runtime secret layer, then Step 7, validate it in dev. (5) Step 8, remove the api_key lines from config/app.yaml and add the CI gate. (6) Step 9, roll out to prod one pod at a time. (7) Step 10, confirm every instance is on the new versions. (8) Step 11, block pre-migration images. (9) Step 12, revoke the old keys one provider at a time. Removing the keys from the file (step 5 here) comes before the prod rollout, and only the revocation at the providers (step 9 here) comes last.

q10.answer: A local run (make run with APP_ENV=dev) reads the sandbox keys from the store path orders-api/dev/* using the developer's own identity under R1. No key is stored on disk or in config/app.yaml, and developers have no read access to prod values. The document leaves open whether each provider actually issues sandbox keys (Q3), and a developer without dev read access cannot run locally until access is granted.

q11.answer: The instance retries the secrets that have not loaded yet, making one attempt plus three retries 2 seconds apart, and only the failed reads are retried. If the missing secret is still absent after the retries, the app logs an error that names the secret and the error class, with no value, and exits non-zero. The orchestrator restarts it with backoff, and it never becomes ready, so the rollout halts and the old pods keep serving. The document does not say how a not-found result differs from a transient read error, so both currently get the same retries and the same exit.
